subject.title: Add backup/restore utility for config, cron jobs, and session history

question: What exact first-party restore/import scope should OpenClaw own for native backups, and which cloud, scheduling, encryption, sync, and migration pieces should stay in plugins or ClawHub?
rationale: The remaining work crosses destructive local state writes, credentials, sessions, archive trust, cron/session merge semantics, and optional integration scope, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Scope Native Restore First
options.body: Define a minimal core restore/import lifecycle for OpenClaw-owned archives with safe extraction, dry-run validation, conflict and rollback rules, and explicit cron/session component semantics, while leaving cloud and scheduled sync to plugins unless a missing API is identified.

options.title: Move Most Scope To ClawHub
options.body: Narrow this issue if maintainers decide community plugin and skill backup flows are sufficient and only docs or plugin APIs should remain in OpenClaw core.

options.title: Design A Full Core Backup Platform
options.body: Accept a broader core design that includes cloud targets, encryption, scheduling, retention, and restore, with a larger security and compatibility review before implementation starts.

recommendation.title: Scope Native Restore First
recommendation.body: Define a minimal core restore/import lifecycle for OpenClaw-owned archives with safe extraction, dry-run validation, conflict and rollback rules, and explicit cron/session component semantics, while leaving cloud and scheduled sync to plugins unless a missing API is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue already has product-routing discussion and needs a core-vs-plugin security boundary decision spanning backup, restore, sessions, cron, and ClawHub scope.
